places.name: Beaumaris Castle
places.ai_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, this perfectly symmetrical medieval castle was built by Edward I but never completed. It features impressive concentric walls, towers, and a moat, showcasing the pinnacle of military architecture in 13th-century Wales.

opening_hours.notes: Hours vary seasonally; check website before visiting.

places.place_tip: Explore the castle walls for panoramic views of the Menai Strait and Snowdonia mountains beyond.
places.address: Castle St, Beaumaris LL58 8AP, United Kingdom

places.name: Beaumaris Gaol & Courthouse
places.ai_summary: A Victorian prison and courthouse complex offering a fascinating glimpse into 19th-century justice and punishment. Visitors can explore cells, the punishment cell, treadmill, and courtroom, experiencing the harsh conditions prisoners endured during this era.

opening_hours.notes: Open weekends and school holidays; check for special events.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the audio guide which brings the prisoner stories vividly to life with atmospheric sound effects.
places.address: Bunkers Hill, Steeple Ln, Beaumaris LL58 8EP, United Kingdom

places.name: Menai Suspension Bridge
places.ai_summary: An engineering marvel designed by Thomas Telford and completed in 1826, this iconic bridge was the world's first modern suspension bridge. Spanning the Menai Strait, it connects Anglesey to mainland Wales with elegant stone towers and graceful suspension chains.

opening_hours.notes: Pedestrian walkway accessible during daylight hours.

places.place_tip: Walk across the pedestrian path for stunning views of the strait and Snowdonia mountains backdrop.
places.address: Menai Bridge LL59 5UY, United Kingdom

attribution.title: Cadnant dingle Jan 2005
attribution.author: [[:en:User:Velela|Andrew Dixon]]
attribution.description: Cadnant Dingle - Menai Bridge, the traditional landing stage for the Bishop of Bangor prior to the construction of Thomas Telford's suspension bridge across the Menai Strait

places.name: Plas Newydd House & Gardens
places.ai_summary: The ancestral home of the Marquesses of Anglesey, this historic house boasts stunning gardens, a rich collection of art and antiques, and breathtaking views over the Menai Strait. The site also features a tearoom and shop.

opening_hours.notes: Last entry one hour before closing. Check for seasonal variations.

places.place_tip: Explore the gardens' woodland walks and enjoy the views from the terrace.
places.address: Plas Newydd, Llanfairpwllgwyngyll LL61 6DQ, United Kingdom

places.name: South Stack Lighthouse
places.ai_summary: Perched on a rocky outcrop, this iconic lighthouse guides ships safely through the waters of the Irish Sea. Visitors can explore the lighthouse, enjoy the dramatic coastal views, and learn about the area's maritime history.

opening_hours.notes: Access to the lighthouse is via a steep, narrow path. Check for seasonal variations in opening times.

places.place_tip: Bring binoculars to spot seabirds and marine life from the cliffs.
places.address: South Stack Rd, Holyhead LL65 1YH, United Kingdom

places.name: Holyhead Mountain & Breakwater Country Park
places.ai_summary: A stunning natural area featuring Holyhead Mountain, the highest point on Anglesey, and the historic Breakwater. The park offers scenic walks, wildlife watching, and panoramic views of the surrounding sea and mountains.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Check weather conditions before visiting.

places.place_tip: Wear sturdy shoes for walking and bring water, especially if climbing Holyhead Mountain.
places.address: Holyhead, Anglesey LL65 1YH, United Kingdom

places.name: Newborough Beach & Llanddwyn Island
places.ai_summary: A beautiful sandy beach leading to the romantic Llanddwyn Island, with its picturesque lighthouse and ruins of a medieval church. The area is rich in wildlife and offers stunning views across the Menai Strait.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Check tide times if planning to visit Llanddwyn Island.

places.place_tip: Explore the dunes and forest area behind the beach for a chance to see red squirrels.
places.address: Newborough, Anglesey LL61 6SG, United Kingdom

places.name: Red Wharf Bay
places.ai_summary: A large, sandy bay popular for its watersports, walking, and birdwatching. The bay is home to a variety of wildlife and offers stunning views, especially at low tide when the sands stretch far out to sea.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Check tide times for best beach access.

places.place_tip: Walk along the beach to explore the rock pools and sandy coves at low tide.
places.address: Red Wharf Bay, Anglesey LL75 8RJ, United Kingdom

places.name: Moelfre Seafront & RNLI Seawatch
places.ai_summary: A picturesque seafront with a sandy beach, rocky coves, and the Moelfre RNLI Lifeboat Station. The area is great for walking, birdwatching, and enjoying the coastal scenery.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Check for RNLI Seawatch times.

places.place_tip: Visit the lifeboat station to learn about the RNLI's work and the history of lifeboating in Moelfre.
places.address: Moelfre, Anglesey LL72 8NN, United Kingdom

places.name: Llynnon Mill
places.ai_summary: The only working windmill in Wales, Llynnon Mill is a restored 18th-century windmill set in beautiful gardens. Visitors can explore the mill, learn about its history and workings, and enjoy the surrounding countryside.

opening_hours.notes: Open weekends and bank holidays; check for special events.

places.place_tip: Check the website for flour sales and special milling demonstrations.
places.address: Llynnon Mill, Llanddeusant, Anglesey LL65 4YH, United Kingdom

places.name: Parys Mountain Copper Mines
places.ai_summary: A fascinating industrial heritage site, the Parys Mountain Copper Mines offer a glimpse into the area's mining history. Visitors can explore the extensive underground tunnels and open-air mine, and learn about the copper mining process.

opening_hours.notes: Last entry one hour before closing. Check for seasonal variations.

places.place_tip: Wear sturdy shoes and bring a flashlight for exploring the underground tunnels.
places.address: Parys Mountain, Amlwch, Anglesey LL68 9RE, United Kingdom

attribution.title: AngleseyCopperStream
attribution.author: Cls14
attribution.description: A stream in the town of Amlwch, Anglesey which is contaminated by acid mine drainage from the former copper mine at nearby Parys Mountain.

places.name: Lligwy Burial Chamber & Din Lligwy
places.ai_summary: An important archaeological site, Lligwy Burial Chamber is a well-preserved Neolithic tomb. Nearby, the Din Lligwy settlement offers a glimpse into Iron Age life, with its hut circles and ancient field systems.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Respect the site and do not disturb the ancient structures.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with a walk to the nearby Lligwy Beach for a complete experience.
places.address: Lligwy, Moelfre, Anglesey LL72 8NH, United Kingdom

places.name: Benllech Beach
places.ai_summary: A popular sandy beach with safe swimming conditions, making it ideal for families. The beach is backed by a promenade with shops, cafes, and beach facilities.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Check tide times for best beach access.

places.place_tip: Explore the rock pools at low tide and enjoy a walk along the coastal path.
places.address: Benllech, Anglesey LL74 8SW, United Kingdom

places.name: Cemaes Bay
places.ai_summary: A charming village and bay with a sandy beach, rock pools, and scenic coastal walks. Cemaes Bay is perfect for a peaceful getaway, with opportunities for fishing, birdwatching, and enjoying the local wildlife.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Check tide times for best beach access.

places.place_tip: Visit the local shops and cafes for a taste of the village's charm and hospitality.
places.address: Cemaes Bay, Anglesey LL67 0NG, United Kingdom

attribution.author: Nicholas Horne from Basingstoke, United Kingdom

places.name: Trearddur Bay
places.ai_summary: A popular seaside resort with a beautiful beach, clear waters, and a range of water sports. Trearddur Bay is ideal for families, with plenty of amenities and activities available.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Check tide times for best beach access.

places.place_tip: Try the local seafood at one of the beachside cafes or restaurants.
places.address: Trearddur Bay, Anglesey LL65 2UN, United Kingdom

attribution.title: Flag of Wales
attribution.author: Unknown  Vector graphics by Tobias Jakobs

places.name: Anglesey Sea Zoo
places.ai_summary: The largest marine aquarium in Wales, Anglesey Sea Zoo is home to a wide variety of marine life. The zoo focuses on conservation and education, offering visitors a chance to learn about and connect with the marine environment.

opening_hours.notes: Last entry one hour before closing. Check for seasonal variations.

places.place_tip: Visit the touch pools and interactive exhibits for a hands-on experience.
places.address: Anglesey Sea Zoo, Brynsiencyn, Anglesey LL61 6TQ, United Kingdom

wikimedia_commons.source_file: File:Castell Mawr, Red Wharf Bay, Benllech - geograph.org.uk - 86150.jpg

attribution.author: Humphrey Bolton
attribution.description: Castell Mawr, Red Wharf Bay, Benllech. Another view of this massive limestone block, the result of limestone quarrying around the site of an Iron-Age fort.  The is the view from the north side, in 1993.  There was at that time a possible way up on the west side (ie to the right in this view), but coming down again would have been difficult, and the undergrowth on top could well be impenetrable.

places.name: Church in the Sea (St Cwyfan’s)
places.ai_summary: A unique and picturesque church located on a small tidal island. St Cwyfan’s Church is accessible by foot during low tide and offers a peaceful and spiritual atmosphere with stunning sea views.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Check tide times for access.

places.place_tip: Bring a camera to capture the stunning views and the unique setting of the church.
places.address: Church in the Sea, St Cwyfan’s, Anglesey LL61 6TQ, United Kingdom

places.name: Penmon Priory & Trwyn Du Lighthouse
places.ai_summary: A historic priory and lighthouse located on the beautiful Penmon Point. The site offers stunning views of the Menai Strait, Puffin Island, and the Great Orme. A peaceful and scenic spot, rich in history and natural beauty.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Respect the site and do not disturb the wildlife.

places.place_tip: Visit the nearby beach and rock pools for a complete coastal experience.
places.address: Penmon, Anglesey LL58 8SW, United Kingdom

places.name: Amlwch Port
places.ai_summary: A historic port with a rich maritime heritage. Amlwch Port offers scenic walks, opportunities for birdwatching, and a chance to explore the local history and geology.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Check local tide times.

places.place_tip: Explore the coastal path for stunning views and keep an eye out for local wildlife.
places.address: Amlwch Port, Anglesey LL68 9AG, United Kingdom

attribution.title: Amlwch Port - geograph.org.uk - 468694
attribution.author: Brian Green
attribution.description: Amlwch Port This view looking northnorth east towards the open sea shows how narrow the port is - a narrow funnel. Before the breakwater was constructed, vessels anchored in the port during a northerly gale were almost certain to suffer severe damage from the 'run' of large waves it generated. In olden times, large balks of timber were hauled across the narrows by winches to form an effective breakwater.

places.name: Cable Bay (Porth Trecastell)
places.ai_summary: A stunning beach with golden sands and clear waters, ideal for swimming, sunbathing, and water sports. The beach is backed by dunes and offers a peaceful and scenic environment.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during daylight hours. Check tide times for best beach access.

places.place_tip: Bring a picnic and enjoy a day on this beautiful beach.
places.address: Cable Bay, Anglesey LL65 2UN, United Kingdom
